title: The Pharisees Controlling Religion
paragraphs:
They looked holy.
But they were strangling people with God’s name on their lips.

The Pharisees did not just love religion.
They loved control.

They built fences around God’s law, then stood at the gate acting like gatekeepers of mercy. They honored rules, but their hearts were cold. They cleaned the outside of the cup while the inside was full of pride, greed, and self-righteousness. Jesus did not stay silent about that. He said, “They tie up heavy burdens, hard to bear, and lay them on people’s shoulders” (Matthew 23:4).

That is the danger of controlling religion.
It looks righteous.
But it crushes souls.

It tells broken people, “Perform first, then maybe God will accept you.”
It majors on appearances.
It weaponizes shame.
It turns worship into pressure and repentance into public theater.

But here’s what we miss: Jesus did not come to protect dead religion.
He came to expose it.

He rebuked the Pharisees not because He hated holiness, but because He loved truth. Real holiness does not control people—it leads them to freedom in God. Real shepherds do not parade power—they carry the weak. Real faith does not make you feel trapped under man-made weight. It drives you to the feet of Christ, where sinners find mercy and the weary find rest.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Because all of us, in some way, are tempted to become little Pharisees—judging others, performing righteousness, craving control, hiding our own need for grace. But Jesus tears the mask off. Not to destroy us. To save us.

The Gospel is this: you are not justified by religious performance, but by the blood of Jesus Christ alone. He fulfilled the law we could never keep. He carried the burden religion could never remove. He welcomed the sinners the Pharisees pushed away. And on the cross, He broke the power of pride, fear, and false holiness.

So do not bow to controlling religion.
Bow to Christ.

He is not a tyrant with a checklist.
He is the Savior with nail-scarred hands.

Come out of spiritual manipulation.
Come out of man-made bondage.
Come out of pretending.

There is freedom in repentance.
There is cleansing in grace.
There is life in Jesus.
